title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Northwest Denver campus places for studying, gathering, recreation, reflection, food, and campus culture.

cards.title: Dayton Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Reserve a library room for a project meeting, then use the group or individual study areas to move work forward between classes.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with reservable rooms plus group and individual study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis states that Dayton Memorial Library provides numerous group and individual study areas and offers library-room reservations.
cards.access_notes: Library access and room reservations are managed by Regis; check the library page for current details.

cards.title: The Ranger Den
cards.subtitle: West Hall patio area, Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Bring a study partner or game group to the couches and group table; the room also has a TV and gaming center for a change of pace.
cards.short_summary: A West Hall hangout with soft seating, games, TV, and a group-study table.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis describes the Ranger Den as having couches, bean bag chairs, a TV, a gaming center, and a group study table.
cards.access_notes: Located off the West Hall patio; access may be governed by University building access policies.

cards.title: Student Center
cards.subtitle: Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Use this campus hub to meet before an event, grab food, or connect a study session with other student activities in the building.
cards.short_summary: The campus activity hub and home to several dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Regis catalog calls the Student Center the center of campus activities, and Regis Dining lists multiple venues there.
cards.source_title: Academic Integrity Policy | Regis University Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Campus facilities are for enrolled students and people engaged in University-sponsored activities; follow building access rules.

cards.title: Regi's Roasts
cards.subtitle: Student Center, Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Pick a seat for coffee, a snack, a study block, or a small team meeting; plan on purchasing food or drinks if you order.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center coffee-and-snack stop with seating for studying or meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis identifies Regi's Roasts as a place for breakfast, coffee, snacks, studying, and team meetings.
cards.access_notes: Dining availability and payment options can change; consult Regis Dining before visiting.

cards.title: Coors Life Direction Center
cards.subtitle: Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Meet friends for intramural activity or use the fitness center’s climbing wall and equipment as part of a planned recreation break.
cards.short_summary: A wellness and recreation hub with fitness, climbing, and intramural activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis says the Coors Life Direction Center includes a fitness center, rock climbing wall, and intramural sports.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current recreation-facility rules and hours.

cards.title: St. John Francis Regis Chapel
cards.subtitle: Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Visit for a quiet moment of reflection or a University Ministry activity, and take time to look closely at the chapel’s art installations.
cards.short_summary: A campus chapel designed for prayer, reflection, faith activities, and art viewing.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis describes the chapel as a space for prayer, reflection, and Faith and Mission activities, with art that supports teaching and worship.
cards.access_notes: Gatherings have specific parameters; contact University Ministry for current access and event information.

cards.title: O'Sullivan Fine Arts Gallery
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building, Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Build a short gallery stop into a walk across campus and use the changing art setting as a conversation prompt with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A named campus gallery in the former chapel building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Regis catalog states that the Fine Arts Building, formerly the chapel, houses the O'Sullivan fine arts gallery.
cards.source_title: Academic Integrity Policy | Regis University Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Check current gallery availability and building access before making a special trip.

cards.title: Main Hall
cards.subtitle: Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Pause at the university’s landmark building while moving between classes, then use its classrooms or conference spaces only as scheduled or permitted.
cards.short_summary: Regis’s first building and an administrative and classroom landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis states that Main Hall was constructed in 1887 as the college's first building and contains administrative offices and classrooms.
cards.source_title: Academic Integrity Policy | Regis University Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Administrative offices, classrooms, and conference rooms may have restricted or scheduled access.

cards.title: Regis Field House
cards.subtitle: Athletics area, Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule, then join or watch an intramural or intercollegiate activity with friends in the campus athletics area.
cards.short_summary: A field house for Regis intramural and intercollegiate sports.
cards.evidence_claim: The Regis catalog says the Field House serves the University's intramural and intercollegiate sports programs and includes a 3,000-seat gymnasium.
cards.source_title: Academic Integrity Policy | Regis University Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Facility access and activity schedules are subject to current athletics and recreation policies.

cards.title: Regis Baseball Field
cards.subtitle: East end of the Northwest Denver campus
cards.notes: Add the baseball field to an athletics-area walk, or attend a scheduled campus game after confirming the event details and entry policy.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic field on Regis’s east end of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Regis identifies the Baseball Field as part of the east end of campus where sports are played.
cards.access_notes: Use the athletics schedule and event guidance for current spectator and facility access.
